summary: Neo Ensemble's chorus with four voices (both machines spread their LFOs evenly round the cycle): the delay swept between Delay − Depth and Delay + Depth lands on the sweep's geometric centre and its octaves, Spread on the right channel's LFO phase, Mix on a crossfade and an output gain.

rules.why: Both in Hz, one sine LFO per voice.

Pedal Chorus sweeps each voice's delay between Delay − Depth and Delay + Depth (straight in time; at least a sample); Neo Ensemble sweeps in octaves round its Delay, an octave either side at 100 %: the same ends, the centre where their ratio is halved.

Pedal Chorus pans its four voices from the centre (0 %) to hard left and right (100 %); Neo Ensemble moves the right channel's LFOs against the left's, the channels differing most at 180°. Both are mono at 0.
Both a one-pole low-pass on the wet sound, in Hz; 20 kHz and above is open on Neo Ensemble (Pedal Chorus's own top, 22 kHz, still takes 0.8 dB off at 22 kHz).

Pedal Chorus crossfades its input with the voices, each from the input's mono sum, panned at equal power and halved: per channel half the power of one voice where Neo Ensemble's voices sum to one voice's power, so its wet counts 0.71 (−3 dB) of Neo Ensemble's, and the output gain keeps the dry level.

remarks: Pedal Chorus sweeps its delay straight in time, Neo Ensemble in octaves: at the same ends Neo Ensemble lingers a little longer on the short delays.
Pedal Chorus pans voices made from the input's mono sum; Neo Ensemble keeps the channels apart and offsets their LFOs, so a stereo input stays stereo in its wet sound.

At wet-heavy mixes with Spread up, one low third octave dips differently (up to 7 dB at Mix 80–100 %, 125 Hz at the defaults): Pedal Chorus's channels hear its panned voices at different levels, Neo Ensemble's hear theirs alike.

tolerance.measured: Linux, Neo Poly noise and chords into it, each side against its input: at its defaults within 0.1 dB, third octaves within 0.8 dB; deep and wide (6 ms on 20 ms, Spread 100 %, Mix 60 %, 1 Hz) within 0.1 dB, bands within 2.2 dB; with Tone at 6 kHz, Spread 0 % or wet only at Spread 0 % within 1 dB
tolerance.why_not: Wet-heavy mixes (above about 60 %) with Spread up dip up to 7 dB more in one low third octave (125 Hz at the defaults, where the voices' delays are a half period apart): Pedal Chorus pans each voice so a channel hears some louder than others, where Neo Ensemble's channels hear all their voices alike, and the voices cancel differently there. At Spread 0 % they match.

evidence: ExternalMachines/source/thepedal/pedal-chorus/PedalChorus.cs (Work: delay = base + sin·depth, voiceGain 2/4, equal-power pans at ±Spread and ±Spread/3, one-pole tone 1 − e^(−2πf/sr))
Machines/NeoEnsemble/Engine/EnsembleEngine.cs (voices averaged times √voices; the right channel's LFO Spread/voices on)
